identity.description: The leaderboard FLOOR for regression: predicts a single constant — the training mean, median, a quantile, or a supplied value — for every row, never reading a feature. Under strategy='mean' it is the R²=0 line by definition: any real regressor must clear it to have learned anything from the features.

consumes.note: X is accepted for API symmetry and IGNORED — only n_samples is read, values are never inspected; the fit consumes y alone (one location statistic of it)

emits.note: the identical constant for every row — mean, median, quantile of y, or the supplied constant

learnsVsFixed.note: strategy-dependent, and deliberately so: mean/median/quantile DO fit — they estimate one location statistic of y (the smallest possible fit); constant learns nothing and is fully specified by its hyperparameter. The component therefore serves both as a trainable floor (refit per leaderboard) and as a fixed reusable reference — hence reusability 'both' even with learns:true

strategy.note: NOT searched on principle — the floor must be a fixed reference; tuning the baseline would move the goalpost. mean is the L2 floor (R² denominator), median the L1 floor

quantile.note: the quantile of y to predict when strategy='quantile'

constant.note: the value to always predict when strategy='constant'

invariances.why: the prediction is one statistic of y; X never enters the computation, so no rescaling of features can change anything
trivially: X is never read, so ANY transform of the features — monotone or not — leaves predictions bit-identical
missing values in X are irrelevant because feature values are never inspected; only the row count is used (NaN in y is a separate reject-input edge case)
raw string categoricals pass through untouched for the same reason — no encoding is ever consulted

no assumption about X (unread) or the target's shape: the mean is the L2-optimal constant under ANY target distribution, the median the L1-optimal — optimality of the constant needs no distributional premise
the only estimate is a single location statistic of y — the lowest-variance fit possible; a handful of rows suffices and cost is one O(n) pass
the output is one constant everywhere; there is no fitted trend to extend beyond the training range — constant, not extrapolated

featureStats.why: the dummy's MSE IS Var(y) under strategy='mean' — exactly the denominator of every candidate's R², so this stat states the floor in the scoreboard's own units
skew is what separates the mean floor from the median floor; a large gap says the loss choice (L2 vs L1) matters before any real model is even fit

modelMetrics.why: equals Var(y) for strategy='mean' — the single number every candidate's skill is normalized by, since R² = 1 − MSE(candidate)/MSE(this floor)
the whole reason this model exists: every leaderboard entry is read relative to this floor, and a gap near zero means the features carry no usable signal for this target

edgeCases.condition: NaN or non-finite values in y
edgeCases.behavior: sklearn raises at fit — the target must be finite
floor MSE = 0 and R² is undefined (0/0) for every candidate — the problem itself is degenerate
the unconditional mean is a misleadingly weak floor — a naive last-value baseline is the honest reference
edgeCases.note: route to the forecasting family's naive floor instead

edgeCases.behavior: the mean floor is inflated by outliers and diverges from the median floor
edgeCases.note: prefer strategy='median' with an MAE scoreboard

placementClaims.why: X is never read; imputation cannot change a prediction that is one statistic of y
no transform of unread features can alter the output — the fit and predict paths touch only y and n_samples
the scale of features that never enter the computation is immaterial by construction
even raw string categoricals pass through — the estimator inspects only the row count, never a feature value
